title: Cherry Blossom Road
description:
April on the Han River cherry blossom road. The flowers were white.
Daeun stopped under the canopy and looked up.
"Minjun, it's like it's snowing." Every gust brought petals down, and she laughed.
An afternoon with no uniform, no register. One petal settled on her shoulder.

description_if_known.cherry_grey_view:
April on the Han River cherry blossom road.
Daeun stopped under the canopy and looked up. "Minjun, it's like it's snowing."
{name} looked up too. It was the first time the cherry blossoms looked grey.
Even {name} knew it wasn't the flowers that had changed.
"...Minjun? Are you okay?" Daeun peered at his face. One petal settled on her shoulder.

choices.text: Brush the petal from her shoulder.
choices.result_text:
When his fingertips touched her shoulder, Daeun smiled a little. "...That tickles."
She caught the petal in her palm. "This year's blossoms — I saw them with you, Minjun."
He wanted to hold onto that sentence for a long time.

choices.text: Say nothing — watch the petals fall together.
choices.result_text:
Neither of them spoke. Falling petals make no sound, but it felt like he could hear them.
"...I've never had a moment like this," Daeun said quietly.
Neither had {name}.

choices.text: "Let's see them together next year too."
choices.result_text:
Daeun's eyes went round, and then she smiled without hiding it.
"...That's a promise now. I remember all of these, you know."
Cherry blossoms last a week. The promise stayed.

title: Cherry Blossom Road
description:
"I even checked the bloom map. This is the peak." Jiyeon led the way.
April on the Han River cherry blossom road. The flowers were white.
She'd picked the route with data, but once under the canopy her steps slowed.
"...Better than I expected." The wind brought petals down, and one landed in her hair.

description_if_known.cherry_grey_view:
"I even checked the bloom map. This is the peak." Jiyeon led the way.
April on the Han River cherry blossom road. {name} looked up.
It was the first time the cherry blossoms looked grey. He knew it wasn't the flowers that had changed.
"Oppa." Jiyeon turned around. "...What's going on in your head these days." Her voice wasn't joking.
A petal landed in her hair.

choices.text: Pick the petal out of her hair.
choices.result_text:
"...What do you think you're doing." She said it without moving away.
The composure that slipped for half a second came right back. "...If there's another one, get that too."
There wasn't. He pretended there was.

choices.text: Say nothing — watch the petals fall together.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon was quiet for a long while.
"...If I were at the office right now, I'd be in my second meeting."
By now {name} knew that was her way of saying it was beautiful.

choices.text: "Let's see them together next year too."
choices.result_text:
"You talk like a project proposal." Jiyeon laughed. "...Approved. Next April, same spot."
She actually put it in her phone calendar.

title: The Sea, After Five Years
description:
The first train to the east coast. The sun was still low. Daeun sat by the window and kept watching the side where the sea would appear. She had come straight from a night shift, yet never once dozed off.

A convenience-store gimbap roll and the route map sat neatly on her lap. Each time she unfolded the map, she checked the window before folding it again.
"Still far?"
"A little. You can sleep if you're tired."
"No. What if I miss the moment it first appears?"

The train entered a long tunnel. Their reflections replaced the view. The night shift still showed beneath Daeun's eyes, but her gaze was bright with the look of someone who had been waiting a very long time for today.

choices.text: "Did you miss it much, all those years you couldn't come?"
choices.result_text:
Daeun did not answer right away. Lights along the tunnel wall swept across her face at even intervals.

"I thought if I let myself miss it, it would feel even farther away." The words came much later. "So I tried not to think about it."

choices.text: Don't ask. Watch the same side of the window with her.
choices.result_text:
{name} leaned toward the glass too. Their shoulders drew closer in the dark reflection.

"You're not going to sleep either, Minjun?"
"How can I when you won't?"
Daeun smiled at the window. He saw it first in the reflection.

title: Five Years of Not Going
description:
The train left the tunnel, and rice fields and low roofs began sliding past again. Daeun pressed her thumb against the corner of the folded route map.

"At first I told myself I'd go next month. Then, next summer."
"And then?"
"Whenever I got a day off, I thought about the money I'd put off. Rent. My mother's hospital bills. Next month's groceries. The sea kept coming last."

Her voice was calm, but the corner of the map had already worn round. For Daeun, five years had not been one great tragedy. They were the sum of small calculations that placed her own turn last every time.

choices.text: "No calculations today. At least until we get there."
choices.result_text:
Daeun looked once at the receipts on her lap, then slipped them into her bag. The route map went on top.

"Okay. Today I'll think only as far as arriving."
The arrival announcement came moments later. Daeun turned to the window before it had even finished.

title: The First Blue Beyond the Glass
description:
The mountains opened for a moment, revealing a blue line in the distance. Daeun leaned so close her forehead nearly touched the window.

"Is that the sea?"
"I think that's a reservoir."
"Oh."
He expected embarrassment. Instead, she laughed. "Then call it practice. Now I won't be as startled when the real one comes."

A few minutes later the blue line returned. This time it had no visible end. Daeun did not ask. She only stared, lips parted. {name} left the answer unsaid and watched her face first.

choices.text: "You found this one first, Daeun."
choices.result_text:
She nodded without looking away.

"Yes. This one's real."
The arrival announcement overlapped her voice. Even as the train slowed, the blue line stayed with them beyond the glass.

title: A Season Returned
description:
Past the shops by the station, they stepped onto the sand. Daeun wore a pale sky-blue shirt over a coral swimsuit. She had checked the price tag several times in the shop, but in front of the sea even the hand worrying at her hem went still.

The salt wind tousled her short hair. Shoes in one hand, Daeun approached the water carefully. The moment the first wave reached her feet, she laughed aloud — a laugh bigger than {name} had ever heard from her, childlike, forgetting even to cover her mouth.

"Minjun, it's been... five years since I saw the sea."
At the end of the words, her throat caught. On the list of things Seoul had quietly taken from her was the sea. This was the face of getting it back after five years.

choices.text: "Next year we're staying overnight."
choices.result_text:
Daeun answered loud enough to beat the waves.
"Okay. ...Promises like that scare me — but if it's you making it, I'm not scared."

On the train back, Daeun fell asleep against the window. A few shells she'd picked up were wrapped in a handkerchief on her lap, and even half-asleep her hand didn't let them go.
As the sea drew away outside the glass, {name} watched her sleeping face for a long time. A day that gave back five years was riding home to Seoul in a handful of palm-sized shells.

choices.text: Say nothing — take her hand and run to the waterline.
choices.result_text:
When {name} took her hand and ran for the water, Daeun grabbed his arm, half scream, half laugh. The instant the cold reached her ankles —
"It's cold! It's c—" and still she didn't step back. "...But I don't want to get out. Just a little longer."

Wet sand held their feet, and each time a wave rushed in and pulled back, the two of them swayed a little. Every time, Daeun gripped {name}'s arm tighter.
Beside someone laughing off five years all at once, {name} just laughed along too — not even noticing his cuffs soaking through with saltwater.

title: Haeundae
description:
The KTX to Busan crossed the Nakdong River. Instead of looking outside, Jiyeon checked the pins saved on her phone again: a market alley, a mulhoe restaurant, the beach entrance, the parasol rental. An itinerary with all the gaps sealed, like a meeting deck.

"Haeundae is my turf."
The end of the sentence lifted with a trace of Busan. It was the hometown accent she almost never let through in Seoul. Unaware of it, Jiyeon continued explaining their reservation time.

The closer the train drew to Busan Station, the clearer the accent became. Without the suit or business card, the woman by the window looked a little less like Han Jiyeon of Seoul and a little more like someone who had left this city long ago.

choices.text: "The moment we reach Busan, even your accent changes."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon stopped mid-explanation. "Nothing about me changed."

The same accent was in that sentence. When {name} smiled, she turned toward the window. The tips of her ears were faintly red in the reflection.

choices.text: "So where are you taking me first?"
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon zoomed in on the map as if she had been waiting to be asked. "The market first. Mulhoe after that. We hit the beach when the crowd thins. I know a cheaper parasol place."

Only the last pin beneath her finger had no name. It sat not out at sea, but exactly where water met sand.

title: Her Hometown Voice
description:
When an attendant passed a moment later, Jiyeon ordered water in precise standard Korean. The low Busan cadence returned only after the attendant had gone.

"Do you deliberately hide it in Seoul?"
"Not deliberately. Let it slip once in a meeting and people spend the rest of it asking where you're from. While I'm trying to talk business."
"Am I allowed to ask?"
Jiyeon looked at {name} in the window reflection. "Oppa, you already followed me all the way here."

After that, she stopped containing the accent. By the arrival announcement, even the station's name sounded different inside her voice.

choices.text: "Then guide me in that voice today."
choices.result_text:
"I'll charge a premium." Jiyeon smiled.

As the train entered the platform, she was the first person on her feet. "Follow me. If you get lost today, that's on me."

title: The Last Pin
description:
{name} pointed to the unnamed pin. "What's this one?"

Jiyeon nearly turned off the screen, then stopped. "Just where we go into the water. The quieter end."
"You plan a separate entry point at a beach?"
"There's nothing wrong with a plan."

Normally another answer would have followed at once. This time there was none. Jiyeon placed the phone face down on her lap and looked outside. The sea had not appeared yet. In the reflection, one finger tapped the edge of the screen.

choices.text: Don't press. Follow her all the way to the last pin.
choices.result_text:
"I'm not scared." The answer came before any question.

{name} only nodded. As the train slowed, Jiyeon turned the phone over again. The last pin was still there.

title: Where Water Meets Sand
description:
Out of Busan Station, through the market and the mulhoe restaurant, they reached Haeundae. Jiyeon traded words with vendors and haggled down the parasol price like someone entirely on home ground.

But when he suggested going into the water, she did not move from beneath the parasol. Arms around her knees, she stared at the sea. The sunglasses stayed on. {name} could not tell where the eyes behind them were looking.

"...Oppa. Don't laugh."
A beat later her voice dropped. "I... can't swim."
The one who had called it her turf wore the face of someone who had never once stepped into that sea.

choices.text: Laugh — try not to, and fail.
choices.result_text:
Watching {name} try not to laugh and fail, "Hey!" — Jiyeon flung a fistful of sand. Her sunglasses slipped a little, and through the gap her eyes shot him a glare. The composure broke for exactly half a second.
"...Growing up in Haeundae doesn't mean everyone can swim." The recovery was quick, as always. She pushed the sunglasses back up, as if nothing had happened.

That day Jiyeon went in only ankle-deep. No further. But in that shallow water, every time a wave came she'd secretly catch {name}'s sleeve — and {name} pretended not to notice.

choices.text: "Then I'll hold on to you. Just to the knees."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon looked at {name} for a long moment over her sunglasses. A weighing kind of silence. Then she took them off. For the first time, her eyes were simply there, bare.
"...To the knees. Cross it and you're dead." And the hand she held out trembled a beat ahead of the waves.

Each time the water touched her knees, that hand tightened. {name} had never seen the proud one grip anything so hard. Not laughing, holding that hand to the end — that was {name}'s only job that day.
On the way back, Jiyeon tossed it out: "...Maybe chest-deep next time." Knowing she wouldn't, and saying it anyway — that was the kind of person she was.

title: Fireworks, a Profile
description:
Yeouido. The fireworks had not begun, but the riverside was already packed. Delivery scooters threaded between picnic mats, while announcements and children's voices mixed in the wind off the river.

At the meeting spot, {name} did not recognize Daeun at first. The one he knew in a convenience-store uniform or plain clothes was wearing a blue-grey dress he had never seen. Her short hair was done differently, and the wind lifted loose strands over light makeup.

"...First time seeing me out of uniform, right?"
Not knowing where to look, Daeun touched the hem and then made herself leave her hand there. Three seconds while {name} chose an answer. The sky was still dark, yet those seconds lasted longer than the first firework.

choices.text: Hold her gaze and ask why she chose this dress.
choices.result_text:
Daeun looked down at the hem as though she had expected anything but that question.

"I just... wanted to wear something other than a uniform today." After a pause she added, "I was a little worried you wouldn't recognize me."

choices.text: Before the crowd surges, move with her toward a quieter stretch of river.
choices.result_text:
{name} opened a path through the crowd. Daeun followed one step behind, and each time a shoulder bumped her, she checked his back before she checked the dress.

Near the railing, they found a gap just wide enough to stand side by side.

title: The Person Outside the Uniform
description:
Daeun admitted that until the moment she left, she had nearly changed into something else. Only after describing how many times she had lifted the dress from the closet and put it back did she seem to realize how much she had said.

"At the store, it doesn't matter what I wear. People only need the name tag."
"And tonight?"
"Tonight... I wanted them to see me first."

The riverside lights caught faintly in the folds of the dress. Daeun stopped worrying at the hem. When a distant announcement warned of the countdown, she looked at {name} first.

choices.text: Keep looking through the three seconds she chooses not to hide.
choices.result_text:
Daeun almost looked away, then stopped herself. For a moment the stream of people between them broke.

"You can tell me if it looks strange."
As the words ended, a low report rolled across the river to signal the first launch.

title: Room for Two
description:
Beyond the railing, apartment lights trembled in long lines across the river. No fireworks yet. Daeun left just enough space that their shoulders did not touch. Every shift in the crowd narrowed it.

"There are so many people."
"Uncomfortable?"
"No." She looked around, then said it quietly. "Even with all of them here, you're the first person I see tonight, Minjun."

She looked more startled than he did by her own words and turned quickly toward the river. Over the speakers, the countdown began to drop one number at a time.

choices.text: When the crowd moves again, keep that space beside her from disappearing.
choices.result_text:
{name} stepped closer and blocked the flow of people with his shoulder. Daeun's arm touched his and did not move away.

"Three, two, one." The crowd became a single voice. Just before Daeun looked up, she glanced once at {name}.

title: The First Firework
description:
When the countdown ended, the first trail of light rose from the middle of the river. The report had not reached them yet. For a moment the whole crowd seemed to draw the same breath.

Daeun looked up, then turned toward {name}. Surprise and laughter shared the same face. The three long seconds from before began again inside that look.

The light reached the highest point of the night. While everyone else faced the sky, only enough space remained between them not to lose each other.

choices.text: "You look beautiful." — before the three seconds run out.
choices.result_text:
"You look beautiful." Before the three seconds ran out, {name} said it.
Daeun tried to hold back a smile and failed. Covering her flushed face with the back of her hand,
"...Even if it's a lie, tonight I'll believe it."
It wasn't a lie. Right then the first firework went off — boom, over the river. Everyone looked up at once, and the light poured down in colors over Daeun's dress, over her laughing face. {name} had no wish to take the words back.

choices.text: When the fireworks burst, watch her profile instead of the sky.
choices.result_text:
Boom — every time the sky lit, color landed on Daeun's face and vanished. Red, green, gold.
Daeun watched the fireworks; {name} watched the one watching them.
"...Minjun, aren't you going to look?" she asked, feeling his gaze.
"I'm looking." An answer given while they watched two different things. A beat later Daeun caught what he meant, and — face turned to the sky — went red to the tips of her ears. And still, not hiding it, she smiled a little.

choices.text: Take her hand before the crowd can push between you.
choices.result_text:
Just before the crowd surged, {name} took Daeun's hand. She startled, looked at him, then squeezed back. Small, but unmistakable.
"If we lose each other, we'll never find our way back," Daeun said, loud enough not to drown in the crowd.
The words carried far past the crowd of that night. As fireworks burst overhead one after another, neither of them let go. Even their palms sweating together was no reason to.

title: Off Duty
description:
The Yeouido fireworks festival. A hand rose above the crowd. It was Jiyeon in a hooded jacket and sneakers, wearing barely any makeup.

No suit, no heels, no business cards. She raised an eyebrow as though timing how long it took {name} to recognize her.
"Four seconds. Longer than I expected."

"People at work would faint if they saw me." Jiyeon pulled the hood lower and smiled. It was not the face of someone ignoring other people's eyes, but of someone freed from them for one night. The sky was still black; only the riverside lights followed their feet.

choices.text: Ask, on purpose, "Where's tonight's schedule?"
choices.result_text:
As if she had been waiting for that question, Jiyeon took out her phone. The whole day was blank on the calendar.

"Nothing. No reservations, reports, or alarms." She turned the screen off. "So don't you check the time either, oppa."

choices.text: Don't judge the unfamiliar clothes. Match her stride.
choices.result_text:
{name} simply took his place beside her. Jiyeon started toward the river, and their sneakers kept the same interval.

About ten steps later she asked, "Why aren't you saying anything? Isn't it strange?"

title: An Empty Calendar
description:
Jiyeon put the dark phone at the very bottom of her bag. With the thing she usually kept in hand gone, both hands looked awkwardly empty. One touched the hood string; the other searched for a pocket.

"Are you really okay doing nothing?"
"Why. Are you nervous?"
"I thought you might be."
"I can fall apart for one day." Jiyeon corrected herself. "No. I can rest."

The crowd began moving toward the river all at once. Jiyeon looked down at her empty hand, then chose not to hide it in her pocket.

choices.text: "Then let's prove nothing tonight."
choices.result_text:
Instead of answering, Jiyeon caught {name}'s sleeve. As more people pressed in, her hand slid from the cuff to his wrist, and from his wrist into his palm.

"It's because of the crowd." The excuse came before she had even finished taking his hand.

title: The Same Stride
description:
"It isn't strange. You don't have to file a report on your day-off clothes."

Jiyeon slowed the half-step she had been walking ahead. "Sometimes you give the correct answer in the least interesting way, oppa."
"Was it wrong?"
"No. That's why it's worse."
The corner of her mouth had already lifted.

Their shoulders were level now. A path she would always have led in office heels, they crossed at the same sneaker pace. Where the riverside entrance narrowed, the back of her hand touched {name}'s.

choices.text: With the backs of their hands still touching, slow down first.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon slowed too. When someone pushed from behind and nearly split them apart, she took {name}'s hand first.

She turned away with a perfectly casual face. "It would be annoying to lose you."

title: The One Who Reached First
description:
As the crowd pressed toward the river, Jiyeon took {name}'s hand first. She tried to make it look casual, but the glance back to check on him was unmistakable. Her hood strings shook in the river wind, and their joined hands drew taut between people.

"It's because of the crowd."
"I didn't say anything."
"You were about to. I'm getting ahead of it."
She faced forward without letting go. Only the warmth in her palm contradicted the excuse.

Far out on the barge, the first trail of light climbed into the sky. In the short silence before the report arrived, Jiyeon started to look up, then turned once more toward {name}.

choices.text: Re-grip her hand — fingers interlaced.
choices.result_text:
When {name} re-gripped her hand with fingers interlaced, Jiyeon glanced down at it. Half a second.
"...It's because of the crowd." The recovery was quick, as always. And still she didn't pull away — if anything, her fingers tightened between his.
The first firework burst over the river. While Jiyeon looked up at the sky, {name} felt only the warmth of that hand. Whatever went off up there, the one certain thing right now was this hand held in his.

choices.text: "I like this version of you better."
choices.result_text:
"I like this version of you better." When {name} said it, Jiyeon stopped walking.
"...Which part." Even in the dark, the red creeping up the tips of her ears under the hood was visible.
"Never mind. Watch the fireworks." A snap — and then she pulled the hood off. The hood she'd kept pulled down, gone at that one line.
Her hair lifted in the river wind, and above it the first firework broke. {name} watched, a long while, the light settling over her uncovered face.

choices.text: When the fireworks burst, watch her profile instead of the sky.
choices.result_text:
Boom — the light repainted Jiyeon's face in shifting colors. Red to gold, then to blue.
Catching {name}'s gaze, she turned. "...What are you looking at."
"The fireworks." "Liar." She smirked — this time without the thorn.
More than the fireworks bursting in the sky, it felt like something quieter had gone off much closer. Jiyeon pretended to watch the sky again, but the held hand stayed exactly as it was.

title: First Snow, That Convenience Store
description:
The first snow came on the way home. Daeun was waiting in front of the convenience store — the one where everything started.

Two small cans of coffee in her hands.
"First snow calls for these." She held one out. "Remember us standing here, just like this?"
The snow was visible only in the light of the sign, then vanished into the dark.

description_if_known.daeun_sea_5years:
The first snow came on the way home. Daeun was waiting in front of the convenience store — the one where everything started.
At the summer sea she said she hadn't seen in five years, he had watched the seasons come back to her one by one. This time it was first snow.

Two small cans of coffee in her hands.
"First snow calls for these." She held one out. "Remember us standing here, just like this?"
The snow was visible only in the light of the sign, then vanished into the dark.

choices.text: "I remember. It was this same coffee."
choices.result_text:
"Right. You looked so... cold back then, Minjun." Daeun laughed, then let the sentence trail off.
"Not anymore. Now you look like someone who's with someone."
Until the cans went cold, neither of them suggested going inside.

choices.text: Say nothing — tap the cans together, like a toast.
choices.result_text:
Clink. The sound of can on can rang small in the snowing alley.
"...What are we toasting to?" "First snow."
Daeun smiled. "Then we'll have to do this every year."

title: The Wipers
description:
The first snow started inside the car on the drive home. The wipers pushed it away twice.

The alley in front of his place. Even with the car stopped, Jiyeon didn't tell him to get out. Then she turned the wipers off.
Snow began to pile on the windshield. The lights smeared away until only the inside of the car was left.
"Oppa, wait," she said. "Let's stay like this."

description_if_known.jiyeon_cant_swim:
The first snow started inside the car on the drive home. The wipers pushed it away twice.

The alley in front of his place. Even with the car stopped, Jiyeon didn't tell him to get out. Then she turned the wipers off.
Snow began to pile on the windshield.
The woman who was afraid of the water was watching the snow pile up to the very end. The same one who never went past the shallows at Haeundae.
"Oppa, wait," she said. "Let's stay like this."

choices.text: Turn off the engine — listen to the snow settling.
choices.result_text:
When the engine died, the world went quiet. Snow makes no sound, but he could almost hear it landing.
"...I'm not the kind of person who does this," Jiyeon said, watching the windshield.
"I know." "...I'm only like this in front of you, oppa."
Until the glass was covered white, neither of them got out.

choices.text: "Want to walk a little, before it melts?"
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon looked at {name}. "...Walking in the first snow? Oppa, you're such an old soul."
She was already unbuckling her seatbelt as she said it.
Under the alley streetlight, two sets of footprints went into the snow first.
